sections.h2: What are the ways to sell in Hurst, TX?
sections.html:
Three routes exist: an agent listing, a private sale, or a direct purchase for cash. Your choice turns on repair needs, debt against the house and your deadline.

Hurst is a compact suburb in the northeast corner of Tarrant County, north of Fort Worth near State Highways 121 and 10. Because the city has almost no raw land left, nearly every sale involves an existing house with some age on it. That favors owners who can show the house well, and it also leaves room for a direct sale when a roof, foundation or kitchen would cost more to fix than a listing would recover.

  • Agent listing: widest exposure, but showings and repair requests after inspection.
  • For-sale-by-owner: no listing fee, but you handle contracts and title paperwork.
  • Cash buyer: fewer steps, usually a shorter timeline, and no repairs.

sections.h2: Why are so many Hurst houses from the postwar years?
sections.html:
Hurst grew late and fast. Farmers settled the area in the 1840s, and the Rock Island railroad arrived in 1903. The stop was first called Ormel, with a post office from 1904 to 1909, before the name Hurst was adopted in 1909, the Handbook of Texas records.

The real change came in 1951, when Bell Aircraft announced a helicopter plant and residents voted 36 to 24 to incorporate, partly to keep Fort Worth from annexing the town. Tarrant County College opened a northeast campus in 1968, North East Mall followed in 1972, and Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport opened in January 1974. By 1970 the population was more than 27,200 and the Handbook estimates about 40,000 in 2020.

That postwar boom explains why so many Hurst houses are fifty to seventy years old. Older houses can carry original wiring, plumbing and slab issues, which buyers will price in.

sections.h2: How did Bell Helicopter and the mall change Hurst?
sections.html:
Employment shaped Hurst's streets as much as the railroad did. The Handbook of Texas says the Bell Helicopter workforce topped 11,000 at the height of the Vietnam War, with many workers building Huey helicopters. In 1958, with 8,500 residents, about half of working Hurst residents commuted to Dallas and about 40 percent to Fort Worth.

Retail followed jobs. North East Mall opened in 1972 and doubled Hurst's retail sales in a month, and it was still the largest mall in Tarrant County in the early 1990s. The Handbook also says Hurst was blocked from growing south by Fort Worth, pursued annexations in other directions from 1956 to 1958, and by the 1970s had nearly reached its limits.

The city's footprint has not changed much since. A Hurst seller is therefore marketing a house in a mature neighborhood with established trees, older lots and close access to employers on both sides of the Trinity River.

sections.h2: Which school district and services cover Hurst?
sections.html:
Hurst, Euless and Bedford share a school district. The Handbook of Texas says the Hurst and Euless districts merged in 1955 and Bedford joined in 1958, and the three cities formed a hospital district in 1969.

When you market a Hurst house, name the school district and the nearby highways, since buyers search by both. The same Handbook entry says Hurst voted to incorporate in 1951 partly to help secure a water supply, and that the Hurst and Euless chambers of commerce merged in 1955 with Bedford joining in 1969. Those ties explain why the three cities are so often named together in listings, school boundaries and hospital services. Anyone selling should also confirm any city permits that apply to completed work, such as a remodel or a fence, by calling the City of Hurst before listing. A permit that was never closed out can slow a buyer's lender.

sections.h2: Which office bills a Hurst homeowner for property tax?
sections.html:
Hurst sits in Tarrant County, so the county Tax Assessor-Collector handles collection. Its main address is 100 E. Weatherford Street in Fort Worth and its phone is 817-884-1100, and the county site says eight branch offices serve taxpayers.

The county tax page also offers a property tax estimator, a list of important tax dates and delinquent tax sale information. A truth-in-taxation database shows the taxes each unit has proposed or adopted for a given parcel.

On its home page, the City of Hurst states that it adopted a tax rate that will raise more maintenance and operations taxes than last year's rate, with an effective increase of 3.51 percent. Read the city's budget notices for the exact rate and treat the county and school figures separately.

sections.h2: What penalties apply to late property taxes in Hurst?
sections.html:
A bill still open after January 31 goes delinquent on February 1. The table follows the Comptroller's schedule.

Late-payment charges on Texas property tax bills (Texas Comptroller)
TimingCharge
February 1Six percent penalty plus one percent interest
Each month after, through JunePenalty grows one percent a month, interest one percent a month
July 1Penalty becomes 12 percent
When an attorney is engagedUp to 20 percent more

Interest never stops at a ceiling. A lien attaches each January and can be enforced against the house after a sale, so unpaid tax worries a buyer's title company as much as it worries you.

sections.h2: What if I am facing foreclosure on a Hurst house?
sections.html:
Lenders in Texas mostly skip the courtroom and use the sale power written into the deed of trust. The State Law Library lays out a fixed clock.

  • A default letter opens a short window to catch up on missed payments.
  • A sale notice follows, posted at the courthouse and filed with the clerk three weeks before the auction.
  • Sales happen on a first Tuesday, and a Hurst house is auctioned in Tarrant County.

Federal rules usually hold a servicer back until a home loan is well past four months behind. A sale that closes first can protect equity and credit, so compare it with the other options and speak with a housing counselor or attorney.

sections.h2: How are deeds and exemptions handled when a Hurst house sells?
sections.html:
Hurst deeds are filed with the Tarrant County clerk, who can quote the records charges for your instrument.

Homestead owners get a $140,000 school deduction and a ten percent yearly cap on appraisal growth, and seniors and disabled owners get an additional $60,000 for school taxes. Mention your exemption status in the sale materials so a lender can estimate the buyer's monthly cost.

sections.h2: What does Texas allow when a Hurst house has unwelcome occupants or a tenant?
sections.html:
Texas treats tenants and squatters differently. A tenant gets written notice to vacate, and the landlord goes to justice court if the tenant stays. A person who entered with no right at all can be handled through Property Code chapter 24B, which lets an owner ask the sheriff or constable for removal, unless the occupant is family or a past or present tenant or a suit is pending.

  • Eviction hearings come within a few weeks of filing.
  • A writ of possession follows only after a final judgment.
  • Wrongful removal can expose an owner to a lawsuit.

Speak with a Tarrant County attorney before filing the request.

faqs.a: Yes. Hurst is in the northeastern quadrant of Tarrant County, just north of Fort Worth, according to the Handbook of Texas.

faqs.q: Whom do I contact about a Hurst tax bill?
faqs.a: The Tarrant County Tax Assessor-Collector, reachable at 817-884-1100 or at the Fort Worth office on East Weatherford Street.
A closing ahead of the auction can pay off the loan and end the process. Start early, because sale dates come monthly.

faqs.q: When does a Texas tax bill go late?
faqs.a: After January 31 in most cases. Penalty and interest begin on February 1.

faqs.q: Must I hire a lawyer to sell in Hurst?
faqs.a: Texas does not make you hire one, yet a lien, a probate matter or a foreclosure notice is a good reason to get legal advice.
